implied_expectations.price_basis: USD 226.27 — the last reported transaction price in a Form 4 filed 2026-09-02 (director Mark A. Stevens, sales 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-02 at $220.06–$226.27). This is a TIER-1 transacted price, preferred here over a tier-4 aggregator quote. Cross-check: a market-cap aggregator reported $5,240B at 2026-09-01, implying roughly $217/share on 24,100M shares — a 4% difference across sources and dates, immaterial to the conclusion.
implied_expectations.shares_basis: FACT (tier-1): 24,100M outstanding at 2026-08-21 per the Q2 FY2027 10-Q cover page.

balance_sheet_2026_07_26_usd_m.note: Marketable debt securities were not isolated in this extraction, so total liquidity is understated here.

earnings_quality_adjustment.why_it_matters: Reported H1 net income ($118,010M) EXCEEDS operating income ($117,270M) because of these gains. Roughly 17-20% of reported net income is investment revaluation, not operations.
earnings_quality_adjustment.core_calculation: H1 pretax $141,410M less $23,707M investment gain = $117,703M core pretax; taxed at the actual 16.5% effective rate gives core net income of roughly $98,282M for the half, $196,564M annualised, or roughly $8.08 of core annualised EPS.

multiples.interpretation: The headline 23.3x is not demanding for a business growing 96%. The honest figure is 28.0x once circular investment gains are stripped. Neither requires bull-case execution — which is why price_requires_unrealistic_bull_case reads PASS. The risk is duration of the earnings base, not the multiple.

future_commitments_2026_07_26_usd_bn.prior_period_comparison: At 2026-01-25 the 10-K disclosed supply and capacity commitments of $95.2B, cloud service agreements $27B, investment commitments $11.4B and other $3.4B — roughly $137B total. Supply and capacity alone rose 193% in six months.
future_commitments_2026_07_26_usd_bn.why_this_is_the_central_risk: Supply commitments of $279B equal roughly 78% of annualised revenue and are the real capital commitment of a business whose reported capex is only 2.8% of revenue. The recorded excess-inventory accrual is $2,138M, so the accounts assume full consumption.

reverse_engineered_requirement.method: Solve for the earnings level that justifies $5,453B at a range of mature multiples, then compare with the current base.
reverse_engineered_requirement.current_base: Annualised reported net income $236B; core net income excluding investment gains $197B.
reverse_engineered_requirement.conclusion: At 25x the price requires roughly the CURRENT core earnings base to persist, with no growth. At 20x it requires roughly 39% growth in core net income. Unlike the Samsung case, the required level is at or near what the business already earns rather than a multiple of any prior peak. THE EXPECTATION GAP IS POSITIVE, THOUGH THIN — and it depends entirely on the durability of a base built on 90% Data Center concentration and $279B of forward supply commitments.

bear.narrative: AI capex digests. Hyperscaler spending — already exceeding those customers' operating cash flow — pauses or is re-phased. The $279B of supply commitments becomes an excess-inventory and cancellation problem, and the $90.7B equity portfolio marks down simultaneously with the demand it financed. Custom ASIC takes incremental share at the top three customers.
bear.note: Severe but not ruinous — the company stays profitable and self-funding throughout. Note the two risks are correlated, not independent: the same demand pause triggers the supply write-down AND the investment mark-down.

base.narrative: Accelerated computing keeps compounding but growth normalises from triple digits toward 20-30%. NVIDIA holds the majority of merchant accelerator share while custom silicon takes the price-sensitive tail. Networking attach continues. Gross margin settles in the low 70s.
base.note: Does not require perfect execution — it requires the installed base to keep expanding and NVIDIA to hold, not extend, its position.

bull.narrative: Accelerated computing becomes the default compute paradigm and the CUDA-plus-NVLink-plus-rack-scale stack holds above 75% of accelerator value. Inference at scale grows faster than training, which favours the installed base. Networking and software become a second and third profit pool.

permanent_loss_case.definition: Permanent impairment of more than 70% of capital, not a drawdown.
permanent_loss_case.required_conditions: Requires a decisive architectural displacement (custom silicon plus an open software stack breaking CUDA lock-in) combined with the supply commitments crystallising as losses, OR a Taiwan supply disruption removing manufacturing access.
permanent_loss_case.why_low: FACT (tier-1): equity $228,984M, liabilities $91,288M against assets $320,272M, H1 operating cash flow $74,421M, capex only 2.8% of revenue. Even the modelled bear leaves the company solidly profitable.

subjective_probabilities.labelled: EXPLICITLY SUBJECTIVE — analyst judgement, not derived from data.
subjective_probabilities.sensitivity_warning: Highly sensitive to the bear weight, which is really a judgement about the durability of hyperscaler capex. At bear 0.20 / base 0.50 / bull 0.30 the weighted return rises to roughly +40% total. At bear 0.40 / base 0.45 / bull 0.15 it falls to roughly +6%. The whole verdict sits inside that range.

notes: Step order per agents/valuation.md: reverse expectations first, then scenarios, then asymmetry, then score. No target price used as a starting point. Every financial input is tier-1 SEC XBRL from the FY2026 10-K and Q2 FY2027 10-Q; the price is a tier-1 Form 4 transacted price. Two material unknowns remain and both are disclosed rather than estimated away: the cancellability terms of the $279B supply commitments, and the share of revenue from entities NVIDIA holds equity in. The asymmetry score is capped structurally — at $5.45T a power-law outcome is arithmetically implausible, so this is a quality-and-duration proposition, not the outlier-magnitude candidate this strategy exists to find.
